headline: TestFlow Agent turns plain English and live website interactions into API tests for Postman, Playwright, and JMeter
summary: TestFlow Agent automates API test creation, generating Postman collections, Playwright API tests, and JMeter plans from either plain English descriptions or recorded browser interactions. This open-source tool streamlines QA workflows, eliminating repetitive m
details: TestFlow Agent is an open-source tool designed to streamline API testing workflows, addressing the common challenge of repeatedly building the same test sequences across different platforms. It aims to eliminate the manual effort of creating Postman collections, Playwright API tests, and JMeter plans for identical business flows.

The first mode allows users to describe their test scenarios in plain English. TestFlow Agent interprets the intent, including states, plans, and test cases, to automatically produce the necessary API sequences. This is ideal for teams with known API structures.

From these descriptions, the agent generates consistent Postman, Playwright, and JMeter artifacts, all sharing the same variables. It also ships with a small mock API, enabling end-to-end execution of the generated flows for immediate validation.

The second, more innovative mode, requires zero prior API knowledge. Users can point TestFlow Agent at any live website, then manually click through their desired workflow within a real browser. The tool records all network traffic during this interaction.

Behind the scenes, TestFlow Agent processes the raw browser traffic, intelligently handling complexities like dynamic IDs, authentication tokens, and chained requests. It then outputs runnable Postman, Playwright, and JMeter tests, complete with resolved variables.

TestFlow Agent is open source under the MIT license, built with Node, Express, and React. It offers a simple one-command Docker setup for quick deployment, making it accessible for developers and QA engineers looking to automate their testing processes.
caption:

The second, more innovative mode, requires zero prior API knowledge. Users can point TestFlow Agent at any live website, then manually click through their desired workflow within a real browser. The tool records all network traffic during this interaction.

Behind the scenes, TestFlow Agent processes the raw browser traffic, intelligently handling complexities like dynamic IDs, authentication tokens, and chained requests. It then outputs runnable Postman, Playwright, and JMeter tests, complete with resolved variables.
